$comment: Agent UI control — the ONE catalog of `otto.ui_*` tools (stdio `otto_ui_*`). Loaded by the daemon (crates/otto-server/src/ui_commands.rs, include_str! + a validation test) and by the UI (ui/src/lib/uiCommands/catalog.ts, a parity test against the registered handlers). Entry fields: name (snake_case, unique; the tool is `otto.ui_<name>`), module (the paneKey — lib/sidePane.ts — of the document that runs it; `shell` = any Otto document, no module needs to be showing), route (the hash route opened when no document shows the module), risk (read | navigate | local_write | outward), timeout_ms (the default deadline the daemon gives the UI; 1000..=120000), headless (optional, `read` only: the daemon-side fallback used when no Otto window can run it — `presence`, `db_list_connections`, `db_mcp_query`), description (what the agent sees), input_schema (a JSON-Schema object: type object, properties, additionalProperties false), $comment (optional, ignored). Blocks: keep each agent's entries together and in order — nav, database (Agent 1 + Agent 4), api/git/browser (Agent 2), the other modules (Agent 5). Arguments named `connection_id` are resolved server-side by id OR name, like otto.query_db_readonly.

commands.name: state
commands.description: Describe what the user's Otto window shows right now: each open document (main pane / side pane), its route and module, whether it is focused/visible, and the current module's own view state. Use it before driving a module. With no Otto window open it returns the daemon's view (`ui_visible:false`).

commands.name: open
commands.description: Open an Otto module (or a specific route inside it) where the user can see it. `placement: side` (default) opens it in the side pane next to your session; `main` navigates the main pane. Returns the route and pane it now shows in.

route.description: Optional hash route inside the module (e.g. `database`, `git/<repo_id>`). Defaults to the module's home route.

commands.name: focus
commands.description: Bring the Otto window to the front and focus a pane (`side` or `main`, default the pane showing the most recently driven module).

commands.name: db_list_connections
commands.description: List the database connections the user can open in the Database Explorer (id, name, kind, environment/guarded flag, workspace). Read-only.

commands.name: db_open_connection
commands.description: Open a connection in the Database Explorer (selecting it in the tree) and optionally make `database` the active database/schema.

database.description: Database / schema / keyspace to make active.

commands.name: db_new_tab
commands.description: Open a new query tab on a connection (attributed to you with an agent chip), optionally prefilled with a statement. Does NOT run it. Returns `{tab_id}`.

database.description: Database / schema to make active for the tab.

commands.name: db_set_statement
commands.description: Replace the statement in a query tab's editor (the user sees it highlighted). Does NOT run it.

commands.name: db_run_query
commands.description: Run a statement in a Database Explorer tab the user can see, and return a result summary plus the first page (≤200 rows, sensitive values redacted). It runs READ-ONLY; a write/DDL asks the user first (and a prod/guarded connection always needs their typed confirm) — a refusal returns `cancelled_by_user`. Pass `tab_id` to run in an existing tab (with `statement` to replace its text first), or `connection_id` + `statement` to open a new tab. With no Otto window open a read-only statement runs headless (`ui_visible:false`).

connection_id.description: Connection id or name — opens a new tab when `tab_id` is omitted.

row_limit.description: The grid's row limit for this run (the rows returned to you are still capped at 200).

timeout_ms.description: Statement timeout. The tool waits up to this + 15 s (max 120 s).

commands.name: db_get_result
commands.description: Read rows of a tab's current result: `{columns, rows, loaded_rows, auto_limited, has_next, elapsed_ms, affected, masked, statement}`. At most 200 rows per call; values are redacted.

commands.name: db_page
commands.description: Move a tab's result grid to the next (`delta: 1`) or previous (`delta: -1`) page, re-running the paged query the user sees. Returns the new page summary.

commands.name: db_set_view
commands.description: Switch how a result is shown (`view`: grid | vertical | json) and/or the Explorer's main tab (`main_tab`: query | structure | diagram | builder).

commands.name: db_open_object
commands.description: Open a schema object (table, view, collection, key…) in the Explorer's tree and object view. `path` is the tree path, e.g. `["shop", "orders"]`.

commands.name: db_explain
commands.description: Show the query plan for a tab's statement (or `statement`) in the Explorer and return it.

commands.name: db_stop
commands.description: Stop a query that is running in a tab.

commands.name: db_export
commands.description: Open the Export dialog for a tab's result, prefilled with `format` and `max_rows`. The USER picks the directory and file name and confirms; returns `{exported, path?}` or `cancelled_by_user`.

max_rows.description: Prefill the row limit (omit for all rows).

commands.name: api_state
commands.description: Describe the API client the user sees: open request tabs (`tab_id`, label, method, url, unsaved flag, saved `request_id`; which one is active), the active environment, all environments, and the saved requests (id, name, method, url, collection). `query` filters the saved requests by name/url. Read-only; secrets are never included.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive filter on saved request name/url.

commands.name: api_open_request
commands.description: Open a saved request in the API client (focuses its tab if it is already open, otherwise opens it without discarding the user's unsaved tabs). Does NOT send it. Returns `{tab_id}`.

request_id.description: Saved request id, or its exact name (otto.ui_api_state).

commands.name: api_set_draft
commands.description: Fill in or edit a request tab where the user can see it. Omit `tab_id` to edit the active tab; `new_tab: true` opens a fresh tab first. Only the fields you pass change; `headers` / `query` REPLACE the tab's lists. Credentials (the Auth tab) cannot be set — reference environment `{{variables}}` instead. Does NOT send. Returns `{tab_id, method, url}`.

commands.name: api_import_curl
commands.description: Parse a curl command into a request tab (the active tab when it holds nothing unsaved, else a new one). Does NOT send it. Returns `{tab_id, method, url}`.

commands.name: api_select_env
commands.description: Make an environment the active one in the API client (its `{{variables}}` fill the next send).

commands.name: api_send
commands.description: Send a request tab (default: the active one) through the API client. The user ALWAYS confirms first — the dialog shows where it goes and what is sent; a refusal returns `cancelled_by_user`. Returns `{status, status_text, duration_ms, headers, body (≤64 KB), body_truncated, tests}`; values are redacted.

commands.name: api_get_response
commands.description: Read the response the API client is showing for the active tab (or `tab_id`, which must be the active tab): status, headers, body (≤ `max_body_chars`, default 64 KB), timing, test results and script logs. Values are redacted.

commands.name: api_save_request
commands.description: Save a request tab (default: the active one) as a saved request — updating it when the tab is already a saved request. The user confirms first. Returns `{request_id, name}`.

collection_id.description: Collection id or exact name; omit for no collection.

commands.name: git_list_repos
commands.description: List the git repositories the user can open on the Git page (id, name, path, workspace, whether it is open as a tab / active).

commands.name: git_open_repo
commands.description: Open a repository as the active tab on the Git page, optionally on a sub-tab (`graph` | `prs` | `review` | `focus`). Returns its current status summary.

repo_id.description: Repo id, or its exact name or path (otto.ui_git_list_repos).

commands.name: git_tab
commands.description: Switch the Git page's sub-tab (`graph` | `prs` | `review` | `focus`) for a repo (default: the active repo).

commands.name: git_status
commands.description: Refresh and return a repo's working-tree status (default: the active repo): branch, upstream, ahead/behind, operation in progress, and the changed files (staged/unstaged/untracked/conflicted). Opens the WIP panel so the user sees the same list.

commands.name: git_diff
commands.description: Show one file's working diff in the WIP panel and return it as unified-diff text (≤ `max_lines`, default 800). `staged: true` returns the staged side of a partially staged file.

commands.name: git_stage
commands.description: Stage (or with `unstage: true`, unstage) files in the WIP panel. The user confirms first. Returns the new status.

commands.name: git_commit
commands.description: Commit the staged changes with `message` (first line = summary). The message is shown in the WIP commit composer and the user confirms first. Signing follows the repo's config. Returns `{sha, status}`.

commands.name: git_fetch
commands.description: Fetch from the remote (like the toolbar's Fetch): updates remote-tracking refs only, never your branches or files. Returns the new ahead/behind.

commands.name: git_pull
commands.description: Pull the current branch (`mode`: merge | rebase | ff_only; default the repo's config). The user confirms first. Conflicts are a normal result (the status lists them). Returns `{status, note?}`.

commands.name: git_push
commands.description: Push (or publish) the current branch to its remote. The user ALWAYS confirms first — the dialog shows the branch, the remote and how many commits go out; a refusal returns `cancelled_by_user`. Returns the new status.

commands.name: browser_state
commands.description: Describe the Browser module: its tabs (id, url, title, mode reader|live; which is active), the active page's title/engine, and the marks (annotations) on it.

commands.name: browser_open
commands.description: Open `url` in a new Browser tab the user can see (`mode`: reader (default) or live). Returns `{tab_id, url, title}`.

commands.name: browser_navigate
commands.description: Navigate a Browser tab (default: the active one; `tab_id` selects it first) to `url`. Returns `{tab_id, url, title}`.

commands.name: browser_select_tab
commands.description: Switch the Browser to one of its tabs.

commands.name: browser_set_mode
commands.description: Switch a Browser tab (default: the active one) between `reader` (fetched, readable text you can mark) and `live` (a real browser view).

commands.name: browser_get_page
commands.description: Return the active Browser tab's page as markdown (≤ `max_chars`, default 20000), with its title and engine.

commands.name: browser_annotate
commands.description: Mark a passage on the active reader-mode page (it highlights like the user's own marks), with an optional `comment`. Locate it with a CSS `selector` (relative to the page article) or `text_contains` (the first paragraph/heading/list item/cell containing that text). The user confirms first. Returns `{annotation_id, selector}`.

commands.name: browser_summarize
commands.description: Summarize the active Browser page (the summary panel shows it to the user, marked as drafted by Otto) and return `{summary}`.

commands.name: k8s_list_clusters
commands.description: List the Kubernetes clusters registered in Otto (id, name, kube context, environment, default namespace), showing the Kubernetes console to the user.

commands.name: k8s_open
commands.description: Open a cluster's workspace in the Kubernetes console on a resource kind (default: the current one, else pods) and optionally a namespace (`""` = all). Returns the namespaces and row count the user now sees.

namespace.description: Namespace to switch to; empty string = all namespaces.

commands.name: k8s_list_resources
commands.description: Show a resource table (cluster + kind + namespace, optional text filter typed into the table's filter box) and return its rows: name, namespace, status, ready, restarts, age, node, health and kind-specific columns (≤200 rows; secrets never carry values).

cluster.description: Cluster id or name. Defaults to the cluster the console shows.

filter.description: Case-insensitive substring over name, namespace, status, node, labels, images.

commands.name: k8s_select
commands.description: Select one resource so its drawer opens beside the table on `tab` (overview | manifest | describe | events | logs | metrics | pods).

commands.name: k8s_describe
commands.description: Open a resource's Describe tab and return the `kubectl describe` text plus its recent events.

commands.name: k8s_logs
commands.description: Open a pod's Logs tab and return its last `tail_lines` log lines (default 200, ≤5000; the text is capped at 60 KB, newest kept).

previous.description: Logs of the previous (crashed) container instance.

commands.name: k8s_action
commands.description: Run a console action on a resource (restart, scale, rollout pause/resume/undo/promote/abort/retry, ArgoCD sync/refresh, CronJob trigger/suspend/resume, delete pod). The drawer opens on the target and the user confirms: an attributed confirm they may allow for the session, but ALWAYS the typed-name confirm for destructive actions (delete pod, rollout undo, scale to 0, prune sync) and on prod clusters. `scale` needs `params.replicas`; `argocd_sync` takes `params.revision` / `params.prune`. Declined → `cancelled_by_user`.

params.description: Action parameters, e.g. {"replicas": 3}, {"full": true} (promote), {"hard": true} (refresh), {"revision": "…", "prune": false} (sync).

commands.name: aws_list_accounts
commands.description: List the AWS accounts registered in Otto (id, name, region, environment, auth mode, which services their IAM allows), showing the AWS page to the user.

commands.name: aws_open
commands.description: Open an AWS account, optionally on a service view (s3 | sqs | ec2 | athena | eks | rds).

commands.name: aws_s3_browse
commands.description: Browse S3 in the user's view: with no `bucket` list the buckets; with `bucket` (+ optional `prefix`) open that folder and return its sub-folders and objects (one level, ≤200).

commands.name: aws_s3_preview
commands.description: Open an S3 object's folder and return a text preview of the object (≤256 KB read, ≤60 KB returned; binary objects return only their content type).

commands.name: aws_sqs_list_queues
commands.description: Open the SQS view and list queues (url, name, fifo) with approximate visible / in-flight message counts for the first 20.

commands.name: aws_ec2_list
commands.description: Open the EC2 view and list instances (id, name, state, type, AZ, IPs, tags; ≤200).

commands.name: aws_sqs_send
commands.description: Send a message to an SQS queue. OUTWARD: the user always confirms (where / what / who) and it is never remembered; declined → `cancelled_by_user`. A FIFO queue needs `group_id`.

commands.$comment: ── Message Brokers / Kafka (Agent 5) — the Brokers page is part of the Connections pane ──
commands.name: brokers_list_clusters
commands.description: List the Kafka clusters in Otto's Message Brokers (id, name, bootstrap servers, environment, read-only flag), showing the Brokers page to the user.

commands.name: brokers_open
commands.description: Open a Kafka cluster tab on a view: overview | topics | groups | schema | replay | alerts.

commands.name: brokers_list_topics
commands.description: Open the cluster's Topics tab and return its topics (name, partitions, replication factor, message count, cleanup policy; ≤200).

commands.name: brokers_list_groups
commands.description: Open the cluster's Consumer Groups tab and return the groups (id, state, protocol type, members).

commands.name: brokers_open_topic
commands.description: Open a topic's detail view (messages, partitions, config, produce) in the Topics tab.

commands.name: brokers_peek
commands.description: Peek messages in the topic's Messages tab — the options land in the user's form and the grid shows the result — and return them (partition, offset, timestamp, decoded key/value, headers; ≤200; sensitive values are redacted before they reach you).

commands.name: brokers_produce
commands.description: Produce one message to a topic. The Produce form is prefilled so the user sees it, then they confirm (attributed; may be allowed for the session). A guarded cluster (prod or read-only) always asks again and is never remembered. Declined → `cancelled_by_user`.

commands.name: vault_list
commands.description: List the vaults (docs homes) and what the Vault page shows: the current vault, its open tabs and open note.

commands.name: vault_open_note
commands.description: Open a note in the user's Vault page (optionally in edit mode) and return its markdown (≤60 KB), title and outgoing links.

vault.description: Vault id or name; default the open vault.

commands.name: vault_search
commands.description: Run a search in the Vault's search panel (full text; `tag:<name>` for a tag) and return the hits (path, title, snippet).

commands.name: vault_write_note
commands.description: Create a markdown note, or replace an existing note's text. An edit is staged in the note's editor first (nothing is saved) and saved only after the user confirms; declining restores the original. Refuses to overwrite a note with the user's unsaved edits. Declined → `cancelled_by_user`.

commands.name: wf_list
commands.description: List the workspace's workflows (id, name, description, step count), the one open in the editor, and the runs in progress.

commands.name: wf_open
commands.description: Open a workflow in the editor (canvas) and return its steps. If the open workflow has unsaved edits the user is asked to discard them; keeping them → `cancelled_by_user`.

commands.name: wf_list_runs
commands.description: Open a workflow and return its recent runs (id, status, started_at; ≤50).

commands.name: wf_open_run
commands.description: Show a run in the workflow's run inspector and return its status and per-step state (status, error, last log lines). Call again to follow a live run.

commands.name: wf_run
commands.description: Run a workflow from its editor (validated and saved first, exactly like the Run button). OUTWARD — its steps can open PRs or post to Slack/Jira — so the user always confirms (where / what / who), never remembered. Returns the started run; follow it with otto.ui_wf_open_run.

input.description: Run input JSON (e.g. working_directory, repos, msg, jira_ticket).

commands.name: wf_cancel_run
commands.description: Cancel a running workflow run (it finishes the current step, then halts). The user confirms (attributed; may be allowed for the session).

commands.name: sched_list
commands.description: List the workspace's scheduled tasks (id, name, kind, provider, schedule, timezone, enabled, where the report is delivered, last status, next run).

commands.name: sched_show_runs
commands.description: Expand a scheduled task's run history on the page and return its recent runs (status, trigger, times, summary, delivery, the session it drove; ≤50).

commands.name: sched_run_now
commands.description: Run a scheduled task once now. The user confirms: an attributed confirm (may be allowed for the session) when the report stays in Otto, but the outward where / what / who confirm, never remembered, when it delivers to Slack / Telegram / email / a webhook.

commands.name: sched_set_enabled
commands.description: Pause (`enabled: false`) or resume (`enabled: true`) a scheduled task, after the user's attributed confirm.

commands.name: home_state
commands.description: Describe the user's Home: its views (spaces 1–4) with their boxes (id, kind, size), the active view, the zoomed box, and which box kinds the user may add.

commands.name: home_go_to_view
commands.description: Switch Home to a view, by 1-based index ("2"), id or name.

commands.name: home_zoom_box
commands.description: Zoom a Home box to fill the page (`zoom: false` returns to the grid).

commands.name: home_add_box
commands.description: Add a live box to a Home view (default the active one) after the user's attributed confirm. Kinds: sessions, mission-control, db-dashboard, k8s, insights, usage (only those the user may view).

config.description: Kind-specific settings (e.g. a DB dashboard id).

commands.name: home_remove_box
commands.description: Remove a box from Home after the user's attributed confirm.

commands.name: swarm_list
commands.description: List the workspace's swarms (id, name, status, description) and which one the Swarm page has open.

commands.name: swarm_open
commands.description: Open a swarm on the Swarm page, optionally selecting a project and a view (tree | graph | kanban | runs | board). Returns its agents, projects and counts.

commands.name: swarm_list_tasks
commands.description: Show the swarm's Kanban board and return its tasks (id, project, title, status, priority, assignee, labels, dependencies; ≤200), optionally for one project / status.

commands.name: swarm_list_runs
commands.description: Show the swarm's Runs view and return its agent runs (id, task, agent, session, kind, status, attempt, summary, error; ≤200).

commands.name: swarm_run_task
commands.description: Run a swarm task now (spawns its agent) after the user's attributed confirm (may be allowed for the session).

commands.name: swarm_stop_run
commands.description: Stop a swarm agent run after the user's attributed confirm.

commands.name: loops_list
commands.description: List the workspace's goal loops (id, name, status, phase, progress, iteration, repo, branch, cost, error).

commands.name: loops_open
commands.description: Open a goal loop's detail page and return its definition and the last 10 iterations (plan, status, evaluation).

commands.name: loops_control
commands.description: Start, pause, resume or stop a goal loop. Start/pause/resume take an attributed confirm (may be allowed for the session); stop can't be undone and always asks.
